title: Infrared project profile
description: Who a project is for, before any infrastructure: what the product is, which environments it runs, how many people use it today and how many are expected. One file per project, `<project>.project.json`, next to `<project>.infra.json` and `<project>.forecast.json`. Hand-written for the mock projects. The expected users are not free numbers: they follow the forecast's traffic scenarios (see `users.expected`), so the profile and the engine never disagree on growth.

project.description: Equals `project` in the infra file and the file-name prefix the orchestrator uses.

summary.description: What the product is and does, in one to three sentences.

owner.description: Team or person that owns the estate.

customers.description: Who pays and who uses it.

critical_flows.description: What must keep working during a migration, in the users' words.

forecast_id.description: `id` of the project's forecast file; the expected users are derived from it.

environments.description: The development environments the project runs. Only the ones that exist; a project without staging lists no staging.

stacks.description: Infra stack ids that make up this environment. A stack whose `environment` is dev, staging or prod must be listed under that environment.

always_on.description: Runs 24x7. false = stopped outside working hours or on demand.

data.description: Where the data in this environment comes from. `copy_of_production` means real customer data outside prod.

users.description: Who uses it, e.g. 'customers', 'QA and two pilot clinics', 'engineers'.

metric.description: What a user count means for this project.

definition.description: Who counts as a user, in plain words.

provenance.description: Same meaning as in infra.json. Mock projects are hand-written, so `synthetic` unless stated.

source.description: Where the number comes from, e.g. 'product analytics, 30-day unique logins'.

peak_concurrent.description: Most users online at once over the last 30 days. Sizes the sandbox's traffic profile.

expected.description: Expected users by month from `current.as_of`, one row per milestone, the last at the forecast's horizon. Each scenario equals current x traffic_multiplier^month x every event traffic_multiplier up to that month, rounded to the nearest 100 (checked by project_integrity.py).
